sections.heading: Two pronouns together
sections.body:
When a sentence has both an indirect object (to whom) and a direct object (what), and you replace both with pronouns, the order is always **indirect before direct**: *Me lo dio.* (He gave it to me.) *Te la mando.* (I'll send it to you.)

Think "**I**D": Indirect, then Direct.

sections.heading: Le and les become se
sections.body:
Spanish never says *le lo* or *les la*. When *le* or *les* comes before *lo, la, los, las*, it changes to *se*:

*Le di el libro a Ana.* → *Se lo di.* (I gave it to her.)
*Les mandé las fotos.* → *Se las mandé.* (I sent them to them.)

Because *se* can mean to him, her, you, or them, add *a* + person if needed: *Se lo di a ella.*

head: Indirect
+ lo / la / los / las
Example
rows: *Me lo explicó.* — He explained it to me.
*¿Te lo digo?* — Shall I tell you?
*se lo, se la, se los, se las*
*Se lo di.* — I gave it to him.
*Nos la trajeron.* — They brought it to us.

sections.heading: Where they go
sections.body:
Both pronouns stay together:

- Before a conjugated verb: *Te lo doy.*
- Attached to an infinitive or gerund (add an accent to keep the stress): *Voy a dártelo* = *Te lo voy a dar*. *Estoy explicándoselo* = *Se lo estoy explicando*.
- Attached to an affirmative command: *¡Dímelo!* (Tell me it! / Tell me!) *Dámelo.* (Give it to me.)

vocab: it to him / her / them / you (formal)
examples: Me lo dio mi hermano.
My brother gave it to me.
Te la mando mañana.
I'll send it to you tomorrow.
Se lo di a Ana.
I gave it to Ana.
Se las mandé ayer.
I sent them to them yesterday.
¿Me lo explicas otra vez?
Can you explain it to me again?
Nos la trajeron a casa.
They brought it to our house.
¿Me pasas la sal? Sí, te la paso.
Can you pass me the salt? Yes, I'll pass it to you.
¿Le diste el paquete a Luis? Sí, se lo di.
Did you give the package to Luis? Yes, I gave it to him.
Voy a dártelo mañana.
I'm going to give it to you tomorrow.
Te lo voy a dar mañana.
I'm going to give it to you tomorrow.
¡Dímelo!
Tell me!
Dámelo, por favor.
Give it to me, please.
¿Me devuelves mi libro? Te lo devuelvo el lunes.
Will you give me back my book? I'll return it to you on Monday.
No se lo digas a nadie.
Don't tell anyone.
¿Quién te dio la llave? Me la dio el portero.
Who gave you the key? The doorman gave it to me.
Se lo estoy explicando.
I'm explaining it to him.
¿Le mandaste la dirección? Todavía no se la mandé.
Did you send her the address? I haven't sent it to her yet.
Mi madre me lo regaló.
My mother gave it to me as a gift.
Nos lo dijeron ayer.
They told us yesterday.
Es un secreto. No te lo puedo decir.
It's a secret. I can't tell you.
¿La contraseña? Te la escribo aquí.
The password? I'll write it for you here.
Se los compré a mis hijos.
I bought them for my kids.

exercises.prompt: *Le di el libro a Ana* with two pronouns is…
Which order is correct?
*Les mandé las fotos* with two pronouns is…
Which is NOT correct?
*Dámelo* means…
Why does *dártelo* have an accent?
options: To keep the stress on *dar* after adding two syllables
All verbs with pronouns have one

exercises.prompt: In *Se lo di a ella*, what does *a ella* do?
My brother gave it to me. (el regalo)
I gave it to Ana. (el libro)
Give it to me, please. (el libro, informal)
Tell me!
They told us yesterday. (lo)
Put the words in order: "It's a secret. I can't tell you."
exercises.answer: Es un secreto. No te lo puedo decir.
